verses.2: Hear from the wise ones from me, and they will know. Listen to me.
verses.3: For then, the ear will hear, and the tongue will taste the food.
verses.4: From the judgment that has been chosen for us, we will know among ourselves what is good.
verses.5: For Iyov said that I am right, and that El will remove my judgment from me.
verses.6: We are ashamed of our judgments; we are half-sinners, yet not fully guilty.
verses.7: Whoever is proud will be laughed at, just like the sea.
verses.8: And he would dwell with the workers of evil, and go with the righteous people.
verses.9: For he said, “Do not harm the vineyard when it is in its bloom with God.”
verses.10: Therefore, O people of Lehavav, listen to me! Save yourselves from evil and murderers.
verses.11: For a man’s work will be rewarded to him, and when a person travels, they will find us.
verses.12: Yet, no one shall be unjustly punished, and no one shall be wronged in accordance with justice.
verses.13: Who appointed him as the ruler of this land? And who placed Egypt under his rule?
verses.14: If his heart, his spirit, and his soul are placed with him, then he will be gathered to him.
verses.15: All flesh shall together be destroyed, and man shall return to dust.
verses.16: And if you understand that this is a call from God.
verses.17: The wicked hate judgment and punishment. But the righteous will be saved.
verses.18: Say to King Belial, the wicked man: “Be generous!”
verses.19: Whoever does not lift his face to women, and who does not show any desire towards them, because his actions are all good.
verses.20: For a moment, they died. Then, in the middle of the night, they were resurrected. The people passed by, and they removed the king’s body, but not with their hands.
verses.21: For his eyes are upon the ways of men, and all their steps he sees.
verses.22: There is no darkness, nor any shadow that can hide those works of evil.
verses.23: For no one should be allowed to go before the judge.
verses.24: The great rulers were unjust and cruel; others stood beneath their rule.
verses.25: Therefore, they will recognize their servants, and it will become night. Then they will be destroyed.
verses.26: Under the wicked, their place is in disgrace.
verses.27: So they abandoned him, and they did not follow any of his ways at all.
verses.28: That he might hear the cries of those who are poor and in need.
verses.29: And he will hide himself; and who can be evil? Who can cover up his sins? Who can harm us, both to nations and to individuals?
verses.30: From King Adam, who was free from the bonds of people.
verses.31: For El Elohim said, “I will not take you away.”
verses.32: Without your help, I cannot succeed. I have tried, but I haven’t succeeded at all.
verses.33: He will give you what you deserve, for you have chosen, and I have not. What do you know about this?
verses.34: The people of Lehav will say to me, “And a wise man who listens to me.”
verses.35: Ioyov does not know how to speak; his words are meaningless.
verses.36: My father will curse Eob for ever, over the sins of the people of Aun.
verses.37: For he adds to his sins; he commits transgressions among us. His words will multiply and increase in number.
